s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk in a patient with a history of systemic sclerosis
salient_findings: Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
Nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles on lesional punch biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis
Patient has a history of heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
Patient is receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Rash is pruritic and has been present for 3 months
Patient denied any known preceding triggers or trauma to the area of the rash
Review of systems was negative for any new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Complete blood cell count with differential was unremarkable
Tissue cultures obtained by punch biopsy were negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, along with the histopathological findings of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers and homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles, is consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis. The absence of skin tightening in the affected areas and the negative tissue cultures also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: Morphea typically presents with skin tightening and sclerosis, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Chronic scleroderma
rejected.why: The patient's history of systemic sclerosis could suggest chronic scleroderma, but the lack of skin tightening and the specific histopathological findings point away from this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: Pityriasis rubra pilaris is characterized by the presence of scale, which is not seen in this patient's rash.

rejected.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
rejected.why: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis is typically associated with renal failure and exposure to gadolinium, neither of which is mentioned in the patient's history.
